related_questions.question: What disqualifies you for an FHA loan?

text_blocks.snippet: FHA loan applications can be denied due to several factors, including low credit scores, high debt-to-income ratios, and issues with the property being purchased. A low credit score (below 580) may require a larger down payment, and some lenders may set even higher minimums. A debt-to-income ratio (DTI) above 43% is often a red flag, and insufficient funds for down payment and closing costs can also lead to denial.

list.snippet: FHA loans generally require a minimum credit score of 580 for a 3.5% down payment.
A score below 580 may require a larger down payment (10% or more) and could be difficult to qualify for with some lenders.
Lenders may have their own credit score requirements beyond the FHA minimum, according to SoFi and Chris Doering Mortgage.
A high DTI, where your monthly debt payments exceed a certain percentage of your gross monthly income, can disqualify you.
FHA typically prefers a DTI of 43% or less, but some lenders may accept higher ratios with compensating factors.

list.title: Insufficient Funds:
list.snippet: You need to demonstrate you have enough money for the down payment, closing costs, and other associated expenses.

list.title: Bankruptcy/Foreclosure:
list.snippet: A recent bankruptcy (within the last two years) or foreclosure (within the last three years) can be a major hurdle.

list.title: Federal Debt:
list.snippet: Delinquent federal debt, like student loans, can also lead to denial, says LendingTree.
Not a Primary Residence: FHA loans are intended for primary residences, not investment properties.
Property Standards: The home must meet FHA's minimum property standards, including safety, security, and soundness, and cannot have major defects, according to Investopedia and Neighbors Bank.
Appraisal: The home must appraise at or above the purchase price, or the deal may fall through.

list.title: Recent Credit Inquiries:
list.snippet: Applying for new credit shortly before or during the FHA loan application process can raise red flags.

list.title: Unpaid Child Support:
list.snippet: Failure to meet child support obligations can also disqualify you, notes FHA.com.

list.title: Existing FHA Loan:
list.snippet: Having one FHA loan may not automatically disqualify you from another, but it can affect your eligibility.
